WITH invoice_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    order_id,
    COUNT(*) as invoice_count
  FROM Invoices
  GROUP BY order_id
),
total_invoices AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) as total_count
  FROM Invoices
),
order_shares AS (
  SELECT 
    invoice_count,
    CAST(invoice_count AS DECIMAL(19,4)) / CAST(total_count AS DECIMAL(19,4)) as share
  FROM invoice_counts
  CROSS JOIN total_invoices
),
average_share AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) as avg_share
  FROM order_shares
),
above_average_orders AS (
  SELECT 
    os.invoice_count,
    os.share,
    av.avg_share
  FROM order_shares os
  CROSS JOIN average_share av
  WHERE os.share > av.avg_share
)
SELECT 
  SUM(invoice_count) as total_number_of_invoices,
  AVG(share) as average_share,
  AVG(share - avg_share) as average_excess_over_average
FROM above_average_orders

assumptions.assumption: Only orders with at least one invoice are considered. Orders with zero invoices are excluded from all calculations of share and average share.

alternatives.interpretation: The second output column 'their average share' refers to the global average share (the threshold they exceed) rather than the local average of only the above-average orders.
